title: api-gateway: consistently emit Retry-After on 429 responses + align SDK error fields
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: As part of the SDK parity initiative (Python/TS/Go), we need the API gateway to reliably communicate backpressure so clients can respect server guidance and avoid retry storms. Today, 429 responses are inconsistent: some routes include Retry-After, others do not; some error bodies omit fields that SDKs use for typed error classification (code/request_id). This PR makes Retry-After emission deterministic for all 429s generated by the gateway rate limiter and harmonizes the JSON error shape consumed by the SDKs. Changes: (1) Always attach a Retry-After header on gateway-generated 429 responses. The value is computed from the limiter reset/next-allowed time and is emitted as delta-seconds (integer, min 1s). (2) Ensure error responses include consistent top-level and nested fields: status, error.code, error.message, error.type, request_id. (3) Add tests covering Retry-After presence/format across REST + streaming handshake paths (i.e., headers returned before body streaming begins) and ensure request_id is propagated. (4) Add metrics + structured logs to support rollout monitoring: gateway_429_total, gateway_429_retry_after_seconds histogram, and logs including request_id, route, customer_id (hashed), and computed retry_after_seconds. Notes/decisions: We intentionally emit delta-seconds (not HTTP-date) to keep SDK parsing uniform; SDKs already support both formats, but we want a single standard server-side. We only set Retry-After for 429 at this time; 503s due to overload remain unchanged (separate follow-up tracked). For pass-through 429s from downstream services, we preserve an existing Retry-After if present, but do not synthesize one (to avoid conflicting guidance). Security: no sensitive identifiers added to logs; customer_id is hashed and request headers are not logged. Rollout: safe to deploy behind the gateway canary first; SRE to monitor 429 rate + retry behavior dashboards during SDK beta. Testing: unit tests for limiter computation + integration tests validating headers and JSON shape. Related: redwood-sdk-* PRs use Retry-After if present and will behave more predictably after this lands.
commits: gateway: compute retry-after from limiter state
gateway: add retry-after header on 429 responses
tests: add integration coverage for 429 + retry-after
obs: add metrics/log fields for 429 retry-after
notable_snippet: Pseudo-diff (illustrative): if resp.StatusCode == 429 { retryAfterSec := max(1, int(math.Ceil(nextAllowed.Sub(now).Seconds()))); w.Header().Set("Retry-After", strconv.Itoa(retryAfterSec)) } writeJSON({"status":429,"error":{"type":"rate_limit","code":"RATE_LIMITED","message":"Rate limit exceeded"},"request_id":reqID})
review_conversation: Allison Grant (SRE): Please ensure Retry-After is ALWAYS present on gateway-generated 429s, including when the limiter rejects before routing. Also add a histogram for emitted values so we can detect pathological values (e.g., 0 or huge).
Ethan Park (author): Updated middleware to set Retry-After on all early-return 429s and added gateway_429_retry_after_seconds histogram. Also clamped to min=1s; max remains limiter-configured window.
Ibrahim Khan (SDK parity TL): Can we standardize the error fields to include request_id at the top level? SDKs currently look for request_id in a couple places and we want one canonical location.

Ethan Park (author): Added request_id as a top-level field across gateway-generated errors. For pass-through errors we keep existing body but inject request_id if missing (without modifying downstream error.code).

Marcus Lin (Security): Avoid logging route params that could contain customer data; also confirm we do not echo API keys in error messages. Please add a test that validates we do not include Authorization in logs on 429.

Ethan Park (author): Logs are structured; we log route template (e.g., /v1/chat/completions) not raw path, and we never log headers. Added a regression test asserting no Authorization is present in error/log payloads produced by the gateway error handler.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/platform): For pass-through 429s, do we overwrite an existing Retry-After header? Some services may already compute it.
Ethan Park (author): We preserve downstream Retry-After if present; only synthesize for gateway limiter 429s. Added a test case for downstream 429 with Retry-After=7.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Looks good. Please add a short note to internal docs describing the contract: Retry-After is delta-seconds int for 429 generated by gateway limiter.
Ethan Park (author): Added docs/internal/gateway-error-shape.md section 'Rate limiting (429) contract' and linked ENG-5130 for follow-ups.
release_notes: Gateway now consistently emits Retry-After on rate-limit (429) responses and returns a standardized error payload including request_id and error.code, improving SDK retry/backoff behavior and debuggability.
